answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a bonded trellis of earned trust: every new identity posts a small copper stake and must complete low-value, verifiably checked work before touching valuable jobs. Each verified delivery adds a rung to its trellis, and the ember of its reputation only glows after a sustained history, not a burst of fresh accounts. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but climbing the trellis takes real work, and one proven fraud burns the stake and collapses the whole trellis. An attacker must do honest work at scale or stay locked out.
